title: U.S. House · New York's 14th District
area: Parts of Queens (Corona, Jackson Heights, East Elmhurst) and the Bronx (Parkchester, Co-op City, Throggs Neck).

context.text: Incumbent Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez defeated Felipe Garcia and Marty Dolan in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary with 86.9% of the vote.
Diamant Hysenaj advanced from the Republican and Conservative Party primaries, both of which were canceled after he was the only candidate remaining on the ballot.

summary.text: Ocasio-Cortez grew up in the Bronx and Yorktown, studied economics and international relations at Boston University, and worked as an educator, organizer, and bartender before defeating Rep. Joseph Crowley in the 2018 Democratic primary. She has represented NY-14 since January 2019 and joined the House Energy and Commerce Committee in 2025. In the 119th Congress she has sponsored or co-led legislation on public housing, health-care corporate consolidation, AI data-center construction, and non-consensual deepfake imagery.

background.text: Born in 1989 in the Parkchester neighborhood of the Bronx; her family later moved to Yorktown, New York, in search of a stronger public school. Her mother was born and raised in Puerto Rico, and her father ran a small business in the Bronx, according to her official biography.
Graduated from Boston University in 2011 with bachelor's degrees in economics and international relations, and interned in the office of Sen. Ted Kennedy during college.

Worked as an educational director with the National Hispanic Institute, helping Latino youth with community leadership and college readiness. After her father died, she worked as a waitress and bartender to support her family, according to her official biography.
Founded Brook Avenue Press, a children's book publisher, and volunteered as an organizer for Bernie Sanders' 2016 presidential campaign in the South Bronx.
In June 2018, defeated incumbent Rep. Joseph Crowley in the Democratic primary and won the general election that November. She was sworn in in January 2019 as the youngest woman to serve in Congress.

Her first piece of legislation in Congress was the Green New Deal resolution; her official biography also lists the Loan Shark Prevention Act, which would cap credit card interest rates at 15%, among her first-term bills.

Served on the Oversight and Government Reform and Financial Services Committees from 2019, and on the Natural Resources Committee in the 118th Congress (2023-2025). She joined the Energy and Commerce Committee in January 2025 and sits on its Energy, Health, and Oversight and Investigations subcommittees.

Belongs to the Congressional Progressive Caucus, Congressional Hispanic Caucus, Medicare for All Caucus, Congressional Renters Caucus, and other House caucuses, and launched the End Corruption Caucus with Reps. Jason Crow and Mike Levin in May 2026.

priorities.text: "Congress has a moral obligation to stand with the American people and stop the expansion of these data centers until we have a framework to adequately address the existential harm AI poses to our society. We must choose humanity over profit."
"I'm proud to co-lead the Stop Corporate Takeovers of Physicians Act to get Wall Street out of Americans' doctors' offices and ban predatory noncompete agreements for healthcare workers."

Co-led the Green New Deal for Public Housing Act to repeal the federal cap on public housing spending and fund large-scale energy retrofits and repairs, which she and co-sponsors say would create an estimated 280,000 union jobs.
Co-led the DEFIANCE Act to give victims of non-consensual, sexually explicit deepfake imagery the right to sue those who produce or distribute it.

positions.summary: In a February 28, 2026 statement on U.S. military operations in Iran, said Congress authorizes war and that she would vote yes on a war powers resolution.
positions.quote: In moments of war, our Constitution is unambiguous: Congress authorizes war. The President does not.

positions.summary: In a July 30, 2025 statement, urged the Senate to pass resolutions blocking the proposed sale of bombs and other weapons to the Israeli government.
positions.quote: The Senate must stop this transfer of weapons, and members of Congress in both chambers must increase pressure on Israel to surge aid into Gaza, hold Netanyahu accountable, and stop sending bombs.

positions.summary: Official issues page says she supports legislation establishing new background check requirements for private-party firearm transfers and a semiautomatic assault weapons ban, and backed the 2022 bipartisan gun law that funds state red-flag programs.
positions.quote: She also supports legislation that would establish new background check requirements for firearm transfers between private parties

record.text: Co-led the reintroduction of the Green New Deal for Public Housing Act with Sen. Bernie Sanders and Rep. Delia Ramirez (introduced August 6, 2026), which would repeal the Faircloth Amendment's cap on new public-housing construction and fund energy retrofits.

Co-led introduction of the Stop Corporate Takeovers of Physicians Act with Sen. Elizabeth Warren, Rep. Val Hoyle, and others (introduced September 16, 2026), which would ban corporate and private-equity ownership of physician practices.

Introduced the House companion to the Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act (H.R. 9442) with Sen. Bernie Sanders (introduced June 24, 2026), which would impose a federal moratorium on new AI data-center construction pending federal safeguards.

Co-led reintroduction of the DEFIANCE Act with Sen. Dick Durbin, Sen. Lindsey Graham, and Rep. Laurel Lee (reintroduced May 2025), which would let victims sue people who knowingly produce or distribute non-consensual, sexually explicit digital forgeries ("deepfakes").
Serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce and its Energy, Health, and Oversight and Investigations subcommittees.

candidates.name: Diamant Hysenaj

summary.text: Hysenaj is a construction-company owner and Kosovo-born immigrant who fled to the Bronx with his family in 1991. He is campaigning on housing, lower health-care costs, immigration, and public safety, arguing Ocasio-Cortez has not been sufficiently present in the district.

background.text: According to his campaign website, born in 1982 on a farm in Kosovo; fled with his family to the Bronx in 1991 at age nine as instability spread across the former Yugoslavia.
Describes working from age 11, delivering newspapers, shoveling snow, and learning the construction trade alongside his father; earned an associate's degree.
Founded a construction company in 2005 that closed during the 2008 financial crisis; says he then worked three jobs, in sales, driving, and construction, to rebuild.

Founded DCG New York Inc. in 2014, which he says has contributed to more than one million square feet of residential and commercial development in New York City. The New York Post described him in June 2025 as president of the firm.

Announced a challenge to Ocasio-Cortez in June 2025. His Republican and Conservative Party primaries were canceled in June 2026, and he is on the November 3, 2026 ballot as the nominee of both parties.
Married since 2017; lives in New York raising two children with his wife, Tereza, according to his campaign website.

priorities.text: "Affordable Rent. Quality Homes. I'm a small business owner in construction, no one knows housing better than me. I have created jobs right here in the district and improved living conditions for everyday New Yorkers."
"Immigration that works. ... I'll demand a system that's tough but fair: secure borders, faster citizenship for the law-abiding, and real support for our neighborhoods."
"Lower your healthcare costs. Get rid of waste and fraud, giving back to the people, not the insurance companies."
"Safe streets, so kids can play outside again."
Says NY-14 needs "a congressperson that is present," criticizing Ocasio-Cortez's national profile and fundraising over what he describes as unaddressed local job losses.

candidates.researchNotes: No Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey or FEC filing summary was available as of research date. His campaign website (home, story and plan pages) was reviewed; only the immigration line qualifies as a statement, and his housing, health care and safety lines do not address the guide's issue statements, so no positions were added.
